rows.comment: Button label that names the action.
"Buzzes on your wrist" is flourish and the curly apostrophe should be straight. State the mechanism: the band keeps the time.
rows.replacement: Buzzes the band at the time you set, using the band's own clock
lineComments: Replaces the wrist imagery with what the alarm does and which clock it uses.

rows.comment: Says when the buzz happens and under what condition.
Possessive "own" and curly apostrophes are filler. The privacy statement stays.
rows.replacement: Counts steps with this phone's sensor for the hours the band does not cover. Nothing leaves the device
lineComments: Keeps the privacy statement and the purpose, with straight quotes and active wording.

rows.comment: Stacked list of three with a vague "off switches for all of them". Name what the screen offers.
rows.replacement: Turn alerts on or off and set quiet hours
lineComments: Says what the reader can do on the screen.

rows.comment: States what the toggle does in each state and that logged data is kept. Useful.
lineComments: Concrete effect of on and off.

rows.comment: Noun fragments in a triad; use verbs the reader can act on.
rows.replacement: Export spreadsheets, make a full backup, or import history
lineComments: Turns the list into the three actions available.

rows.comment: "Events out" is jargon and the "cannot be triggered by it" clause is hard to parse. State each platform's capability.
rows.replacement: On Android, band events can trigger automations. On iOS, Shortcuts can buzz the band, but band events cannot trigger Shortcuts
lineComments: Splits the platform difference into two direct statements.

rows.comment: Colloquial "say so" and passive. Privacy meaning stays: nothing is sent without consent.
rows.replacement: Sends nothing until you allow it
lineComments: Same privacy statement, active voice, plain word.

rows.comment: "Nothing about you goes with it" contradicts the longer lookup text in app_localizations_en.dart, which says the site sees the barcode and your IP address. Add the IP fact.
rows.replacement: Sends each scanned barcode to openfoodfacts.org, which also sees your IP address. Nothing else about you is sent
lineComments: Names the data that does leave: the barcode and the IP address, matching the detailed lookup text.

rows.comment: Privacy statement with concrete scope and conditions (whole database, daily, Wi-Fi, charging). Do not weaken.
lineComments: States what is uploaded, when, and why.

rows.comment: Gives the problem and the recovery step.
lineComments: Says the build is too old and where to get the new one.

rows.replacement: A newer build is available on GitHub

rows.comment: Privacy statement naming what the server sees. Concrete.
"Who this app is not" rebuts a claim nobody made and does not name the content.
rows.replacement: Disclaimers, data sources and open-source licences

rows.comment: Describes what the gallery shows. Developer-facing and accurate.
lineComments: Concrete scope: text scales and themes.

rows.comment: "May interrupt you" is vague. Say what the screen controls.
rows.replacement: WHICH ALERTS YOU GET

rows.comment: "The OS lets it" is vague and does not say what to do.
rows.replacement: No alert below arrives until you allow notifications in system settings.

rows.comment: Gives a limit (one a day) and the trigger (a change from your baseline).
"Gone quiet" and "on the charger" are terse and ambiguous. Name the events.
rows.replacement: Low battery, charging started, and no data from the band

rows.comment: Em dash and the "silent otherwise" fragment.
rows.replacement: A 7pm reminder on nights with no wake alarm set. Sends nothing when an alarm is set
lineComments: Two plain sentences, same time and condition.

rows.replacement: One notification when your morning recovery score is ready

rows.comment: "Most weeks are quiet" is an unsupported claim and "actually found something" is filler.
rows.replacement: Sunday evening, only when the week had a finding. Sends nothing otherwise
lineComments: Keeps the schedule and the condition, drops the unchecked claim.

rows.comment: "Efforts the band spotted" and "goes on measuring either way" are loose. Say what is asked and what Off does.
rows.replacement: Asks you to confirm workouts the band detected that you did not start. Off hides the prompt and the review cards. The band keeps recording

rows.comment: Em dash. Thresholds (two hours, 90 minutes) are kept.
rows.replacement: Nudges you after a still stretch: two hours with no movement, or 90 minutes in a desk posture. Sends a phone notification, and buzzes the band while it is connected
lineComments: Same thresholds, colon before the list, no em dash.

rows.comment: "Kept clear of" is vague and the sentence is dense. Numbers kept.
rows.replacement: A reminder about 45 minutes before the bedtime learned from your own nights. It stays outside your quiet hours and starts after about a week of wear
lineComments: Splits into two sentences with the same 45 minutes and one week.

rows.comment: States the trigger and the once-a-day limit.
Em dash and passive "Nothing is sent". The skip rule stays.
rows.replacement: One notification per scheduled dose at the times you entered, plus a buzz on the band if it is connected. A dose already marked taken or skipped sends nothing
lineComments: Same rules, no em dash, active voice.

rows.comment: Em dash and "write the day" is figurative.
rows.replacement: One evening prompt to log mood, energy and stress. Skipped if the day already has a rating
lineComments: Names the action and the skip condition.

rows.comment: "Nothing is measured either way" is passive and unclear. Say the app does not measure intake.
rows.replacement: Buzzes the strap and notifies your phone during your waking hours so you log a drink. The app does not measure what you drink
lineComments: Active voice and a clear statement of what the app does not measure.
